p2_b2.ocr: The accompanying data table elucidates key metrics relevant to the evaluation of such evidence, specifically focusing on the order of proof and the application of the CDMBE framework. The order of proof serves as a foundational construct, delineating the sequence in which evidence must be presented to substantiate the prosecution's assertions. This structured approach ensures that the jury or judge can systematically assess the credibility and relevance of the evidence provided.

p2_b3.ocr: Additionally, the incorporation of the CDMBE (Case-Dependent Model of Burden of Evidence) further enhances the understanding of the evidential landscape by quantifying the burden placed on the prosecution at various stages of the trial. By analyzing these components alongside the Fenton model, which offers a probabilistic framework for evaluating evidence strength, legal professionals can better navigate the complexities of case presentations. Collectively, these metrics facilitate a more rigorous examination of the prosecution's strategy and its effectiveness in achieving a favorable verdict, thereby underscoring the importance of methodical evidence presentation in the pursuit of justice.
